title: Low Resolution Images in Your Book: How to Fix the 300 DPI Error | SparkPrep
h1: How to fix low-resolution (under 300 DPI) images in your book
description: Printer warned your images are below 300 DPI? Learn what DPI means for print, how to check it, and how to keep Word, Canva and InDesign from shrinking your images.
platforms: Amazon KDP · IngramSpark · Barnes & Noble Press · Lulu
lead: A picture that looks sharp on your screen can still print blurry. Printers want 300 DPI, and many programs quietly lower it.
errorNote: Paraphrased. KDP shows this as a low-resolution image warning in its previewer.
why:
DPI (dots per inch) is how much detail an image has for its printed size. Screens need about 72 to 150. Print needs 300 DPI at the size the picture appears in the book.

So a 1200 x 1800 pixel photo is sharp printed at 4" x 6", but blurry stretched across a full 6" x 9" page. Word and some PDF tools also shrink images when saving, which drops a good picture below 300.

steps: Pixels needed = inches x 300. A full 6.125" x 9.25" cover with bleed needs about 1838 x 2775 pixels.
If your image is smaller than that, get a bigger version from the original source.
File → Options → Advanced → Image Size and Quality.
Tick Do not compress images in file and set Default resolution to High fidelity.
Re-insert the original images, then save as PDF.
Download as PDF Print, not PDF Standard.
Don't stretch a small photo to fill a large area.
Window → Links shows each image's Effective PPI. Aim for 300 or more.
When exporting, under Compression, don't downsample below 300.

faq.q: What DPI do I need for a printed book?
faq.a: 300 DPI at the size the image is printed. Lower resolution prints soft or pixelated.

faq.q: How many pixels for a 6x9 book cover?
faq.a: At 300 DPI, the front alone with bleed needs about 1838 by 2775 pixels. The full wrap is wider because it includes the back and spine.

manual: Open your original file and find every picture.
For each one, divide its width in pixels by its printed width in inches. Under 300 means it will print soft or blurry.
Replace it with a bigger original, or make it smaller on the page. Stretching it bigger in Word or Canva doesn't add detail.
Turn off image compression before you export (Word: File → Options → Advanced → "Do not compress images in file"), then re-export the PDF.
Re-upload it to your printer and wait for the file review again. If it fails, you start over.
